title: How item performance varies with board and trait context

cases.title: Gunblade behind Juggernauts
cases.subject: items
cases.original_question: Does Gunblade become a better item on Zyra when she's playing behind Juggernauts, or do those boards just do well regardless of her build?
cases.question: Does Gunblade become a better item on Zyra when she's playing behind Juggernauts, or do those boards just do well regardless of her build?
cases.scenario: Zyra2 with three ordinary completed items. Compare Gunblade versus supported alternative thirds sharing the other pair, separately in lower, four and six Juggernaut contexts.
cases.plan: Discover Zyra loadouts, then use holder-bound compare_cohorts within each verified Juggernaut contribution interval. Condition named Maokai presence, Summoner activation and tank/carry investment where support permits. Inspect count/level distributions with query_cohort.
cases.checks: Evaluate the item contrast within each context before discussing whether it differs across contexts; report cell sizes and mean/top4/win. A strong Gunblade+Juggernaut marginal alone cannot establish the interaction. Difference-of-differences is a descriptive derived comparison; no native interaction significance test exists.
cases.limits: No generic all-healing-source control, combat healing or universal matched-board budget. Trait medal alone cannot encode four versus six.

cases.title: Elise carry pair without the emblem
cases.subject: items
cases.original_question: Is Rageblade–Titan's Elise actually good in ordinary Vanguard boards, or does it only look good when she has a Ravager emblem?
cases.question: Is Rageblade–Titan's Elise actually good in ordinary Vanguard boards, or does it only look good when she has a Ravager emblem?
cases.scenario: Elise3 with three items, split four/six Vanguard. Ordinary Rageblade/Titan's plus an ordinary third is distinct from Rageblade/Titan's/Ravager Emblem with active Ravager. Elise2 is a separate sensitivity.
cases.plan: Discover exact Elise loadouts and compare ordinary carry alternatives inside Vanguard strata, then inspect the emblem-bearing complete package with the emblem explicitly bound to Elise and Ravager active. Keep the one-holder guard and exact third item visible; do not silently replace Titan's with an emblem.
cases.checks: Report within-context build outcomes, counts and the ordinary versus emblem package difference, with the lost ordinary third slot stated. Judge whether ordinary builds have supported outcomes rather than requiring the emblem hypothesis to win.
cases.limits: Ordinary-only on Elise can be established by exact triplet identity; global no-special-items cannot be assumed. Coven rewards, acquisition and damage role are not observed.

cases.title: Red Buff inside Inferno
cases.subject: items
cases.original_question: Does Red Buff still improve Ashe's endgame results when the board already has Inferno, or is its good average mostly coming from boards without that trait?
cases.question: Does Red Buff still improve Ashe's endgame results when the board already has Inferno, or is its good average mostly coming from boards without that trait?
cases.scenario: Fully itemized Ashe at one and two stars separately; Red Buff versus an observed alternative third sharing the other pair, within active Inferno strata and genuinely without-active-Inferno boards.
cases.plan: Use rank_unit_loadouts to discover comparable trios. For each build, compare active Inferno to its complement within the Ashe build shell to include boards with no Inferno row. Use explicit build comparisons in active contribution strata and report differences; do not implement missing-trait absence with active:false alone. Track Inferno Emblem on Ashe separately.
cases.checks: Cross build and trait context instead of using Red Buff's pooled average. Report star-specific cell support, mean/top4/win and available uncertainty. Distinguish native allied trait activation, emblem consumption of a slot, and other named burn equipment.
cases.limits: A complement supplies a valid inactive-or-absent summary but cannot be reused as a general nested filter; fully crossed no-Inferno build contrasts may need separate complements with descriptive comparison. No opponent burn coverage or exact combat overlap is measurable.

cases.title: Morgana utility and the second carry
cases.subject: items
cases.original_question: Is Morello–Void Staff Morgana a good build on her own, or do its results depend on having a fully itemized Ahri beside her?
cases.question: Is Morello–Void Staff Morgana a good build on her own, or do its results depend on having a fully itemized Ahri beside her?
cases.scenario: Morgana2 with three ordinary items: Morello/Void Staff plus an explicit third versus observed damage trios, crossing Ahri2 with three items, Ahri underitemized, another named AP carry, and no such itemized carry.
cases.plan: Discover exact loadouts and candidate partners. Compare holder builds with compare_cohorts inside named Invoker/frontline shells. Define partner investment with UnitCondition item counts/stars; exclude a bounded named AP-carry candidate set only if complete for the declared pool. Query total equipment and other holder loadouts descriptively.
cases.checks: Separate Morgana's own build association from the partner association and give cell counts/outcomes. Define 'on her own' as no other declared fully itemized AP carry, not no other units. Statikk is an artifact candidate, not ordinary Void Staff equivalence.
cases.limits: No generic AP-role predicate, no global item-budget matching, and no inference of actual damage share. Candidate-pool-limited absence must be labeled.

cases.title: Mama Beak across board families
cases.subject: items
cases.original_question: Does Titan's actually beat Kraken on carry Mama Beak in Summoner boards, and does that still hold when she's played in a Riftbeast-heavy board?
cases.question: Does Titan's actually beat Kraken on carry Mama Beak in Summoner boards, and does that still hold when she's played in a Riftbeast-heavy board?
cases.scenario: Mama Beak3 with three ordinary items first; Titan's versus Kraken with a supported shared pair. Two-star results separate. Summoner and Riftbeast contexts can overlap.
cases.plan: Discover loadouts, query each named trait's contribution rows, then explicitly condition both trait intervals to create joint cells. Compare exact holder triplets within those cells and common named carry/frontline conditions. Inspect two-star cells separately.
cases.checks: Keep hybrids visible; do not pretend Summoner and Riftbeast are exclusive families. Report within-cell build counts and mean/top4/win before discussing variation across families; itemized carry conditions exclude naked trait fillers.
cases.limits: Alpha Mark ownership is not exposed and cannot be inferred from the cohort. Joint trait cells need conjunctive filters, not two marginal trait rows.

cases.title: Seeker’s and trait-provided stats
cases.subject: items
cases.original_question: Is Seeker's Armguard worse than Crownguard on Fiddlesticks when I play lots of Defenders and Spellweavers, or do the results still favor it there?
cases.question: Is Seeker's Armguard worse than Crownguard on Fiddlesticks when I play lots of Defenders and Spellweavers, or do the results still favor it there?
cases.scenario: Fiddlesticks3 with Adaptive Helm/Titan's, varying Seeker's Armguard versus ordinary Crownguard; repeat two-star separately and cross Defender/Spellweaver support.
cases.plan: Resolve artifact versus ordinary identities, discover fixed-pair loadouts and compare exact one-copy holder trios in explicit joint Defender/Spellweaver contribution strata. Preserve Flora Fatalis and Soraka conditions where visible and inspect other special-item holders.
cases.checks: Report counts and placement/top4/win effects for the fixed pair, including uncertainty. Do not collapse trait contexts or attribute any effect to armor/AP saturation, takedown stacks or duration. A wider pair comparison is a labeled sensitivity only.
cases.limits: Artifact acquisition and exact whole-board artifact count are not cohort filters. They remain residual selection differences even with equal holder item counts.
